ratings.comment: I liked what he was trying to do.  He was thoughtful.  He chose a readable text, assigned interesting problems from it (many routine), and then complemented the material in lecture - the lectures added to the text, not simply reproduced it.  They added to it by connecting topics from calc 3 with differential geometry or proving different facts.
avoid at all costs
he's a nice guy.  he can be unclear at times (like most teachers), but he is willing to help and is a very reasonable grader.  exams are fair.
Horrible professor and very boring.  Also the curve was ridiculous near impossible to get an A or AB.

AMAZING professor to take if you learn from the book like I do. It was a match made in heaven, i never went to class, only read the book and was 100% prepared.....quite the obvious if you cant learn from a book and especially if you dont have a good TA.
Avoid
Looks at the chalkboard and talks the whole time. Can't understand a word this guy says. If you like yourself, don't take him.

Lectures are dumb and pointless.  He rarely looks at the students and merely copies examples from the text book.  TA's are great.  I did not go to lecture once and got an AB for the course.  This class is easy if your TA is good and you have friends to help you.  Math is universal....find people that have taken Calc and your golden.

The midterms were fine, but the final was ridiculous.  It did not reflect what I learned.  I studied for hours, but the final was impossible.  Do not take a class with this professor.  He taught a concept that wasn't even in the book in the last class before the final.
ok wow. his first two tests were ok but the final was impossible. he gave out a list of sample problems of basically what NOT to study.
Avoid this professor! The worst professor I have ever had hands down!

I just took the final in this class..it did not at all reflect what we learned this semester. I understand making a final reasonably difficult, but this was just beyond comprehension. I studied for HOURS, and none of it could have prepared me for what I would see on the test. PLEASE, save yourself the bade a grade and take someone else!

not clear on what he said.  he stutters and jumps all over.  when you ask him to explain something he just confuses you more.  I learned the majority of my "knowledge" from my TA's.  take the other professor!!

Technically, Professor Kalafat really didn't teach once during the entire course.  The authors of the text book should really look into suing Prof. Kalafat for copyright infringement, considering the fact he copied Chapters 1 - 7 entirely on the black board throughout the semester.

If you have to take calculus, find another teacher. The lectures are brutal and he just copies directly from the book and stares at the blackboard. The material isn't hard but you are going to end up teaching yourself

By about the third week, 1/3 of the class was was not there, and halfway through about 2/3 did not show up. Not because they dropped the course, the reason is his lectures are useless. Final was packed, if you take this class, better hope you have a good TA

Classic example of a Professor who is here to research, and is reluctantly forced to teach. His exams aren't as easy as other's have expressed, and grade distribution is extremely skewed. Getting above a BC, for even the best of students is extremely challenging, but on the flip side it's hard to get much lower than that.
Examples are useful, tests and syllabus are fair, and always available for extra help.  I would highly recommend him.

Lecture was a disaster. I stopped going after the first midterm and never regretted it. Teach yourself from the book and BUY THE SOLUTIONS MANUAL. Ok class if you're good enough at math to learn it on your own. Don't even think about taking it if you're terrible at math. You'll spend many stressful hours looking at your math book.

Lecture was kind of pointless to attend as he just copies out of the book. Tests are very straightforward, though. He gives many example problems for preparation. He seems very reserved and quiet, but he was easily accessible and responded to emails quickly.

I got A's on both midterms and the final...and I never went to lecture.  Don't go, honestly its a waste. BUT my tip for success: read textbook and learn info by doing odd problems (then check solution with solution-book) When you go to buy the textbook, the solution-book is optional...GET IT! trust me. It shows you every step. tests aren't hard.

The lectures are extremely boring -- but if you aren't into reading the book on your own -- you copy all the examples from the book into your notes.  Homework & Exams are extremely bearable...and he does not throw ANY curveballs.  Bad lecturer, but good professor in terms of testing knowledge of Calculus.

Class is not too hard. It is very much dependent on your TA. My TA was very good and quite easy. If you do the homework you should be able to do well. Also, his exams are almost directly taken from the problems that he posts before each exam. The exams were very fair and straight forward. If you have to take Math 211, I recommend Kalafat!

Very unpersonable, unhelpful professor. Stands at board slowly copying down example problems from the book, and mumbles along. Attending discussion is your only hope. Don't waste your time going to lecture- you won't learn anything.
Worst professor I have ever had in college. Has no interest in teaching basic level calculus whatsoever. Horrible.

Horrible lectures!!  Many days it's hard to keep up because he writes so fast on the chalkboard.  When learning new material he constantly mumbles through proofs that no one cares about unless you major/minor in math.  Your TA helps you out A LOT!!  It's really hard to get less than a C or B/C, even if you don't attend class often.
If you truly hate yourself, take this class
terrible

This is the worst Professor at UW-you can't understand what he says, he copies the book onto the board, only wrong, and doesn't really explain anything. Basically you have to teach yourself out of the book-TAs are ok, but generally refuse to reteach what he does. Tests are difficult if you didn't take calc in high school-avoid like the the plague

The professor rarely acknowledges that he has a class full of students. He is more interested in writing on the board. He not personable at all, and I feel like going to lecture is a complete waste of time.

The teacher is boring, I have to agree. He also isn't a great teacher but if you do the assigned problems from your TA and generally understand the material you will get a good grade. The tests are really easy and are only based on fundamental concepts. There are NO curve balls.

Easily the worst professor I will ever have here at UW. Not only does he make his lectures unbearable, but he makes plenty of mistakes himself in doing impossible problems for the class. He spends most of his time (when he's not confusing the class) erasing letters and lines on the board to make it look nice. He loves math, but not the kids in it.

This guy is awful. I only met one person who actually didn't mind him. You better be able to teach yourself math out of the book, because you will not learn anything from him. Woarst teacher I have ever had
Guy reads right out of the book and then writes it on the board. Look to your TA's for help.

Read out of the text book, copied it onto the board extremely slowly. Writes really slow, seems like he has OCD to write perfect letters, erasing and re-erasing multiple times. Pauses while speaking many times and overall does not help at all. Reading the text is more useful, class is a waste. I like math, and would not recommend taking 340.
Really bad teacher. He read straight out of the textbook for the entire class. He doesn't like to answer questions, and seems extremely flustered at times.

Horrible prof. Showed up 5-10 minutes late nearly every day, so that probably added up to a week of class missed over the course of the semester. Pretty much just read right out of the book, so if you don't understand the book you're screwed.
